title: Operational Icons on Color Backgrounds
slide_intent: Adapt icon contrast to the packaging field while retaining meaningful exceptions so ingredient information stays distinguishable.
strategic_value: White reversals with controlled cheese and spicy highlights can keep Burger King packaging readable and consistent across product colors.
demonstration: An orange panel shows a labeled grid of white icons plus highlighted cheese and spicy variants; the left copy specifies reversal, exceptions and size limits.
practical_value: Reverse operational icons to white on colored packaging and apply the separate cheese and spicy highlight rules.

content_islands.name: Background rules
content_islands.spec: Place the reversal rule, highlight exceptions and size interval in the left column.

content_islands.name: White icon panel
content_islands.spec: Use an orange rectangle behind rows of captioned reversed ingredient and operational symbols.

content_islands.name: Highlighted variants
content_islands.spec: Place orange-cheese, yellow-cheese and red-spicy icons on white circles at the lower right of the panel.

reference_purposes.Expression: The orange panel shows white silhouettes with isolated colored highlights.
reference_purposes.Application: The copy defines the white reversal and distinguishes Whopper-with-cheese from other cheese-wrap treatments.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Cheese and spicy highlights use white circles; Whopper cheese is Flaming Orange, other colored wraps use Melty Yellow cheese, and spicy remains red. Icons stay 24–84 pt with consistent height.

ingredient.name: Operational icon reversals
ingredient.role: Keep packaging symbols legible and distinguish special ingredient markers.
ingredient.application: On colored packaging reverse icons to white. Highlight cheese and spicy on white circles: Flaming Orange cheese for Whopper sandwiches with cheese, Melty Yellow cheese for other colored wraps, Fiery Red spicy on all colored packaging.
ingredient.scope: Historical packaging rule; preserve 24–84 pt consistent-height limits and the named product exceptions.
